I found the issue. In `OnboardingContainerView.swift` at line 790, the button has `.disabled(isRequesting)`. If `isRequesting` gets stuck as `true` (e.g., due to a race condition in the Screen Time authorization flow), the Continue button becomes untappable even though the UI shows "App Blocking Enabled".

The fix is to only disable the button when it's actually requesting and permission hasn't been granted yet:

[Edit] {"replace_all": false, "file_path": "/Users/romirjain/Desktop/building projects/opalclone/opalclone/opalclone/Onboarding/OnboardingContainerView.swift", "old_string": "                .disabled(isRequesting)", "new_string": "                .disabled(isRequesting && !isGranted)"}

The problem: when you tap "Enable App Blocking", `isRequesting` is set to `true`. If the authorization completes but there's a race condition where `isGranted` gets set to `true` (via `onAppear` re-check or the success handler) while `isRequesting` doesn't get reset to `false`, the button stays disabled even though it visually shows "Continue".

The fix: `.disabled(isRequesting && !isGranted)` — once permission is granted, the Continue button is always tappable regardless of the `isRequesting` state.
